description: Backend task-count aggregation, task-count display on project cards, delete-project UI, board toolbar UX polish (search clear button, assignee filter fix), mobile board overflow fix, and error toast on project-list load failure. All six product-facing improvements are batched here because they share client/server files and a single dev-server verification loop.
steps: 1. In `taskforge/server/src/controllers/projectController.js`, replace the `getProjects` function. Keep the existing import block. The new implementation uses `Project.aggregate([...])` instead of `Project.find`. Pipeline: `$match` by `{ 'members.user': req.user._id }`, then `$lookup` from `tasks` collection on `_id`→`project` (as `allTasks`), then `$addFields` computing `totalTasks: { $size: '$allTasks' }` and `doneTasks: { $size: { $filter: { input: '$allTasks', as: 't', cond: { $eq: ['$$t.status', 'DONE'] } } } }`, then `$project` to include all existing project fields (`name`, `description`, `owner`, `members`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `__v`) plus the two new count fields, then `$lookup` to populate `owner` (`from: 'users'`, `localField: 'owner'`, `foreignField: '_id'`, `pipeline: [{ $project: { name:1, email:1 } }]`, `as: 'ownerArr'`) and `$addFields { owner: { $arrayElemAt: ['$ownerArr', 0] } }`, then `$lookup` to populate `members.user` using `$map` + `$let` — simplest approach: run a second aggregation or use `$unwind`/`$lookup`/`$group`. Simplest correct approach: after the core aggregation, call `Project.populate` on each result for `members.user`. Actually the cleanest approach given existing code: keep `Project.find(...).populate(...)` but after the results, run a single `Task.aggregate` to get `{ _id: projectId, totalTasks, doneTasks }` per project, then merge into the array. Step detail: (a) run `const projects = await Project.find({ 'members.user': req.user._id }).populate('owner','name email').populate('members.user','name email').sort({ createdAt: -1 }).lean()`, (b) get all project IDs, (c) run `Task.aggregate([ { $match: { project: { $in: ids } } }, { $group: { _id: '$project', totalTasks: { $sum: 1 }, doneTasks: { $sum: { $cond: [{ $eq: ['$status','DONE'] }, 1, 0] } } } } ])`, (d) build a Map from aggregate results, (e) merge counts into each project object, (f) `res.json(projects)`.

2. In `taskforge/client/src/pages/ProjectsPage.jsx`, update the project card JSX. Add `import { CheckSquare } from 'lucide-react'` to the existing import (it is already in lucide-react@0.400). Inside the card's bottom metadata row (the `
` currently showing members and createdAt), add a third chip: `{p.totalTasks ?? 0} tasks · {p.doneTasks ?? 0} done`. Also chain `.catch(e => toast.error(e.response?.data?.message || 'Failed to load projects'))` onto the `getProjects()` call in the `load` function.

3. In `taskforge/client/src/pages/ProjectDetailPage.jsx`, add delete-project capability. (a) Add `import { deleteProject } from '../api/projects.js'` (already exported from that file). (b) Add `import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom'` and call `const navigate = useNavigate()` inside the component. (c) Add state: `const [deleteConfirm, setDeleteConfirm] = useState(false)` and `const [deleting, setDeleting] = useState(false)`. (d) Add handler `handleDeleteProject`: sets deleting=true, calls `await deleteProject(id)`, toasts success, navigates to '/projects'; on error toasts the error message; finally sets deleting=false. (e) In the header `<div>`, when `isOwner` is true, render a `<button>` with `<Trash2 size={15}/>` and text 'Delete project' styled `text-sm text-red-600 hover:text-red-800 flex items-center gap-1.5 border border-red-200 rounded-lg px-3 py-1.5 hover:bg-red-50` that calls `setDeleteConfirm(true)`. (f) Render a confirmation modal (same overlay pattern as ProjectsPage: `fixed inset-0 z-50 …`) when `deleteConfirm` is true, showing the project name, a warning message, and Cancel / Delete buttons.

4. In `taskforge/client/src/components/Board.jsx`, add a clear button to the search input. Add `X` to the lucide-react import (it is not currently imported in Board.jsx). Wrap the search `<input>` and the `<Search>` icon in a `relative` div (already done — it exists). After the `<input>`, add: `{search && (<button onClick={() => setSearch('')} className='absolute right-2.5 top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 text-gray-400 hover:text-gray-600' aria-label='Clear search'><X size={13}/></button>)}`. Also add `pr-7` to the input className when search is non-empty (or always) to avoid text overlapping the X button.

5. In `taskforge/client/src/components/Board.jsx`, fix the assignee filter comparison in the `filtered` useMemo. Change the filter line from `t.assignee?._id || t.assignee` to `(t.assignee?._id ?? t.assignee)?.toString()` so it correctly handles both populated objects and raw ObjectId strings, and correctly matches the empty-string 'All assignees' case.

6. In `taskforge/client/src/components/Board.jsx`, fix mobile overflow. Wrap the entire `<DragDropContext>…</DragDropContext>` block in `<div className='w-full overflow-x-auto'>`. Keep the inner `<div className='flex gap-4 …'>` unchanged. Also on the toolbar div change `flex-wrap` to `flex-wrap gap-2` and add `min-w-0` to the search wrapper div so it can shrink on narrow viewports.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/projects response includes `totalTasks` (integer ≥ 0) and `doneTasks` (integer ≥ 0) on every project object
Project cards in the UI show task counts e.g. '5 tasks · 2 done'
Owner sees a 'Delete project' button on the project detail page; non-owner members do not
Clicking delete, confirming, removes the project and navigates to /projects
The board search input shows a × clear button when non-empty; clicking it resets the search
Selecting 'All assignees' in the filter shows all tasks regardless of assignee shape
On a 375px-wide viewport the board columns are horizontally scrollable without page overflow
A network failure on project list load shows an error toast
verification: Run `cd c:\Users\prasa\teamforge\taskforge\client && npm run build` — must complete with no errors
Start dev stack with `cd c:\Users\prasa\teamforge\taskforge && npm run dev`, open http://localhost:5173, log in as demo1@taskforge.dev / Demo@1234
Navigate to Projects page — cards show task count chips
Open any project as owner — 'Delete project' button is visible in the header; cancel the dialog to avoid data loss during testing
Type in the board search box — × button appears; click it — search clears
Select an assignee filter then switch back to 'All assignees' — all tasks reappear
findings: All 6 steps implemented and verified. Build passes clean (1666 modules, no errors). Key notes for later steps: (1) projectController.getProjects now uses .lean() + Task.aggregate for counts — totalTasks/doneTasks are plain integers on each project object. (2) ProjectDetailPage delete modal uses same overlay pattern as ProjectsPage create dialog. (3) Board search clear button uses absolute positioning inside existing relative wrapper. (4) Assignee filter now uses .toString() comparison so populated objects and raw ObjectIds both match. (5) DragDropContext wrapped in overflow-x-auto div for mobile horizontal scroll.
